headline: ICT orders Sheikh Hasina and 29 others to surrender by Sept 16
summary: The International Crimes Tribunal has directed authorities to publish notices for the ousted prime minister and other high-ranking officials over the 2013 Shapla Chattar crackdown.
details: The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) has ordered ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, former army chief Gen (retd) Aziz Ahmed, and former IGP Benazir Ahmed, along with 27 others, to appear before the court by September 16.
The order comes after the prosecution informed the tribunal that 30 of the accused, including the former prime minister, could not be found at their respective addresses.
The case involves the crackdown on Hefazat-e-Islam activists at Motijheel's Shapla Chattar in Dhaka and in Narayanganj on May 5-6, 2013.

The tribunal had previously issued arrest warrants against the absconding accused. On July 27, the ICT accepted formal charges of genocide and crimes against humanity against Sheikh Hasina and 38 others.
If the accused fail to appear or cannot be traced, the tribunal will appoint state-appointed lawyers to represent them and conduct the defense based on relevant documents.
caption:
Sheikh Hasina and 29 others ordered to surrender by Sept 16.

The case involves the crackdown on Hefazat-e-Islam activists at Motijheel's Shapla Chattar in Dhaka and in Narayanganj on May 5-6, 2013.

The tribunal had previously issued arrest warrants against the absconding accused. On July 27, the ICT accepted formal charges of genocide and crimes against humanity against Sheikh Hasina and 38 others.

If the accused fail to appear or cannot be traced, the tribunal will appoint state-appointed lawyers to represent them and conduct the defense based on relevant documents.

headline_marked: 1,252 hospitalised in 24 hours as [[4 more die of dengue]]
headline: 1,252 hospitalised in 24 hours as 4 more die of dengue
summary: Total dengue deaths in Bangladesh have risen to 111, with over 39,000 cases recorded so far this year.
details: At least four dengue patients died and 1,252 others were hospitalised in 24 hours ending at 8:00am today, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
The deaths were reported in Dhaka North City Corporation, Dhaka South City Corporation, Khulna, and Chattogram divisions.
With these latest figures, the total number of dengue deaths in the country has risen to 111, while the total number of cases has reached 39,532.
Currently, 2,954 dengue patients are undergoing treatment in hospitals across Bangladesh.
